def: Sliding a small grid of weights over an input and summing the products at each position to produce a map of how strongly a pattern is present.
The small grid of learned weights, also called a kernel, that a convolutional layer slides over its input.
The grid of filter responses produced by one filter over an input, showing where its pattern was found.
Reusing the same weights at every position of the input, so the parameter count does not grow with the input size.
An assumption built into a model's structure, such as locality in a convolution, that helps it learn from less data but limits what it can easily represent.
Adding a border of zeros around the input so that edge pixels are covered as often as central ones and the output keeps its size.
The number of pixels a filter moves between positions, where larger strides give smaller outputs.
The region of the input that can influence one unit's value, which grows as layers are stacked.
Replacing each small window of a feature map by a single summary value such as its maximum or mean.
Collapsing a whole feature map to one number per channel, which discards position.
The property that shifting the input shifts the output feature map by the same amount.
A skip path that adds a block's input to its output, so the block learns a correction and gradients flow through the addition.
